title: GDGoC Bowen Kickoff and Info Session
summary: Meet the leads, see what the chapter is planning this session and find the team that fits you.
description: The opening session of the year, where every track introduces itself and you get a feel for what GDGoC Bowen actually does across the session. Come whether you are a first year or a final year, there is no prior experience expected.
learn: How to join a project team
What the year ahead looks like

title: Git and GitHub for Beginners
summary: Commit, branch and push your first project, and learn the workflow every team expects you to know.
description: We start from an empty folder and finish with a project on GitHub and a pull request. Bring a laptop with Git installed, we will help you fix the setup on the day.

title: Flutter Study Jam
summary: Build a small cross-platform app with Flutter, step by step, with mentors on hand.
description: Follow a guided path from a blank Flutter project to a working app with lists, navigation and basic state. Mentors move around the room to unblock you, so no one gets stuck for long.

title: Cloud Study Jam: Ship a Site with Firebase
summary: Take a finished front-end project and put it on the internet with Firebase Hosting in one afternoon.
description: Bring a project you have already built and leave the session with it live on a real URL. We cover the Firebase CLI, deploying, and using preview channels for changes.

title: Figma to Frontend: Design Handoff Clinic
summary: Designers and developers work through a real handoff together, from Figma file to working page.
description: Most projects stumble at the handoff between design and code. In this clinic, pairs take one Figma file and turn it into a responsive page, talking through spacing and states as they go.
learn: Reading a Figma file like a developer
Designing states beyond the happy path

title: Build with AI: Your First Gemini API App
summary: Call the Gemini API from a simple web app and ship a small AI feature you can show off.
description: We build a small study assistant from scratch, starting with an API key and ending with a working feature you can put on a portfolio. You need basic JavaScript, everything else is covered in the session.
learn: Getting and protecting an API key
Wiring a model into a web page

title: React Weekend Bootcamp: Build a Real App
summary: A full day of React fundamentals, ending with a deployed app that fetches real data.
description: From components and props to hooks, routing and data fetching, you build one app across the day and deploy it before you leave. You should know HTML, CSS and basic JavaScript coming in.

title: Deploy Your First App on Google Cloud
summary: Containerise a small app and run it on Cloud Run without touching a server.
description: A gentle first look at cloud deployment. We package a small Node app in a container, deploy it to Cloud Run, and look at logs and scaling together.
learn: What a container is and why it helps

title: Android Kickstart with Kotlin
summary: Write your first Android app in Kotlin and Jetpack Compose and run it on a real device.
description: We set up Android Studio, cover the Kotlin basics you actually need, and build a simple app with Jetpack Compose. Bring a cable if you want to run it on your own phone.

title: First Internship Panel: Getting Hired in Tech
summary: Alumni and industry engineers share how they landed their first roles, and what they would do differently.
description: A panel of people who have been through the process, applications, interviews, SIWES placements and first jobs. The second half is all Q and A, so bring your questions.
learn: What recruiters look for in a portfolio

title: Intro to Machine Learning with TensorFlow
summary: Train and test a simple model in the browser and learn how machine learning actually works.
description: No heavy maths required. We train a small image classifier step by step, look at what it gets wrong, and talk about why. A laptop with a modern browser is all you need.

title: GDGoC Bowen Hack Night
summary: Form a team, pick a problem on campus and build a working prototype in one evening.
description: Teams of three or four build a prototype that solves a real problem for Bowen students, with mentors from every track on hand. Each team demos what they built at the end.
learn: Scoping a project in one evening
Working as a team in one repo
